text:
Priya: Heads-up — spun up a local test image for acceptance tests and hit a weird redwoodctl auth failure. The container image baked ~/.redwood as root, so the CLI can't persist profiles.
Marco: Which image? Is this the official redwoodctl deb package in our CI image?
Priya: Yep, ubuntu:22.04 base + apt install redwoodctl in Dockerfile. The install step ran as root (obvs), so /root/.redwood exists and is root:root. When the non-root test user runs redwoodctl it tries to write ~/.redwood/profiles.json and fails with EACCES.
Taylor: Oof. We should detect existing ~/.redwood owned by other uid and surface a clear error. Right now redwoodctl prints a vague "fs error" and exits.
Priya: Paste from container log: 
```
2025-02-12T02:14:01Z auth: starting device code flow
2025-02-12T02:14:07Z auth: got device_code, polling
2025-02-12T02:14:10Z auth: poll: unauthorized
2025-02-12T02:14:10Z fs: open /home/testuser/.redwood/profiles.json: permission denied
2025-02-12T02:14:10Z runtime: fatal: unable to persist profile
```
Marco: That's actionable. Two ways to fix: (1) Dockerfile postinstall step chown to the intended user, (2) redwoodctl should check and give a helpful message like "~/.redwood is owned by uid 0; run chown or reinstall without root" and an automated --fix flag for CI.
CLI QA: Adding note: some customers will run system-level installs in golden images and then run the service as non-root. This will be a recurring pain. We should include a recommended Dockerfile fragment in docs.
Priya: My quick workaround in the build image: after apt install run `chown -R 1000:1000 /home/testuser/.redwood || true`. That unblocks tests.
Taylor: I'll file an internal ticket to add a clearer error and a `redwoodctl doctor` check that validates ~/.redwood ownership and perms. Also propose `redwoodctl install --system` to declare system install semantics (writes /etc/redwood for system-wide configs) vs per-user.
devops-bot: Issue created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwoodctl/issues/5278 — "installer: handle system-level installs and detect ~/ .redwood ownership in CI images" (label: devex, priority: medium)
Marco: Another edge: localserve mounts the host dir into container and the UID mapping means files appear owned by host uid. Add guidance for mapping in compose examples.
Priya: For now the test image patch is merged — changed Dockerfile + docs blurb in our repo. Will follow up if more customers file similar bugs.
CLI QA: Thanks — assigning follow-ups to Taylor for doctor + error text and Marco for docs examples.
Priya: Closing the loop — this was surprisingly noisy to debug in CI, so happy we have a ticket.
